name: Pink Floyd Cafe
why_it_matters: Highest cafe in Tosh village — Pink Floyd posters, Floyd on the speakers, and a clear-day view down the valley to the Parvati glacier. The most-photographed sunset spot in Tosh; also doubles as a guesthouse with rooms above.
insider_tip: It's a 15-minute uphill scramble from upper Tosh — wear shoes, not sandals. Skip the EDM nights; afternoon (3-5pm) is when the mountain light is at its best.
signature_address: Upper Tosh village, near Manikaran, Tosh 175105, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh

name: Stonedage Cafe & Inn
why_it_matters: Built by hand at 2,500m at the very edge of Tosh — every brick carried up by foot and mule from Barshaini. Wood-fire kitchen, three hand-built cottages, and Rick the co-founder usually around the bonfire after dinner.
insider_tip: It's at the 'end of the road' end of Tosh — first-time visitors take 45 minutes from the village entrance. Book ahead; only 3 cottages and 2 dorms exist.
signature_address: Upper Tosh village, end of the road, Tosh 175105, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh

name: Boom Shiva Cafe
why_it_matters: 360-degree glacier views from a circular wood deck — rooms ring the perimeter, the campfire and music live in the middle. The cafe Tosh trekkers are sent to when they ask for 'somewhere with a view'.
insider_tip: Ask for the corner table facing the glacier — it's claimed by sunset regulars from 4pm. Village shops are 10 minutes downhill if you need anything not on the menu.
signature_address: Tosh village, Tosh 175105, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh

name: Olive Garden Classic
why_it_matters: A 19-room guesthouse-cafe ten minutes' walk from central Tosh — quieter than the Pink Floyd / Boom Shiva crowd, pure-veg kitchen, the easier sit-down option for families coming up from Kasol.
insider_tip: It's pure-veg only — meat-eaters should go to Boom Shiva or Pink Floyd. The terrace catches morning sun first; ideal for breakfast before a Tosh-glacier day-hike.
signature_address: Central Tosh, Tosh 175105, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh

name: Parvati Tales Cafe & Beds
signature_dish: continental breakfast on the forest deck
why_it_matters: Cafe-and-beds at the literal edge of Pulga's Fairy Forest — pine-tree views, BBQ pit, packed-lunch service for trekkers heading deeper. Hosts an annual 'Parvati Tales Festival' inside the Fairy Forest itself.
insider_tip: Order a packed lunch the night before if you're walking to Tulga or up to Kheerganga the next day — they make sandwiches and parathas to-order from 7am.
signature_address: Edge of Fairy Forest, Pulga village, near Barshaini, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105

name: Holy Cow Cafe & Beds
why_it_matters: At the upper end of Kalga settlement — forest in front, snow-covered Parvati peaks behind. Run by a manager-cook who'll set up a bonfire on request. Reliably the best-rated kitchen in this trio of Pulga-Tulga-Kalga.
insider_tip: Kalga's apple village identity is real — ask if the day's compote or tart is from village orchards (Sept-Oct best). Washrooms are spotless, a rarity above Barshaini.
signature_address: Upper Kalga village, near Barshaini, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105

name: Shalom Waterfall Cafe
why_it_matters: The halfway dhaba on the Barshaini-Kheerganga trail — beside a gushing waterfall, with basic stay rooms upstairs. Where every Kheerganga trekker stops to refill, eat Maggi, and drink the watermelon juice.
insider_tip: Trail prices roughly double Kasol's — budget ₹100 for a Maggi, ₹300 for the watermelon juice. Cash only; there's no signal up here for UPI on most days.
signature_address: Halfway point, Kheerganga trekking trail, between Rudranag and the summit, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh

name: Kheer Ganga Trekking Camps
why_it_matters: One of the named tent-camps clustered at the Kheerganga summit meadow, ten minutes from Parvati Kund hot spring. Public dining tent — meals included for staying trekkers, walk-ins fed when there's room.
insider_tip: All cooked food at the summit is hauled up on mules from Barshaini; menus shrink after September snow. Eat before the 4pm cloud-rolls or you'll be queueing in the cold.
signature_address: Kheerganga summit meadow, Nakthan, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105

name: Jim Morrison Cafe
why_it_matters: On the Kasol-Chalal trail — tribute cafe to the Doors frontman, with low cushion seating, dreamcatchers, graffiti walls and dorm beds upstairs. The most-Instagrammed cafe in Parvati Valley after Pink Floyd Tosh.
insider_tip: It's a short uphill from the Chalal trail; the climb filters out the half-committed. Cushion-floor area fills by 6pm — get there before 5 for a window-side spot for the sunset.
signature_address: Kasol-Chalal trail, Chalal village, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105

name: Shanti Cafe Chalal
why_it_matters: Riverside cafe-and-hostel in Chalal village proper — Parvati-river-facing balcony rooms, Italian-leaning menu, and one of the few places in Chalal with proper pasta done right (not Maggi-with-ketchup).
insider_tip: Sit on the balcony, not inside — the Parvati's roar is loud enough that the inside seating feels muffled. Pasta portions are big; one plate plus garlic bread feeds two.
signature_address: Chalal village, Kasol-Chalal trail, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105

name: Evergreen Cafe Chalal
why_it_matters: Long-running Chalal cafe with the most-affordable Israeli plates in the village — actual hummus, actual pita, no shortcut chickpea-paste-with-curd. Tables on a small lawn under apple trees.
insider_tip: Cheapest hummus in the valley but no menu surprises — order the basics and skip the 'Mexican' fusion attempts. Cash works; UPI is spotty under the tree canopy.
signature_address: Chalal village, Kasol-Chalal trail, Kullu District, Himachal Pradesh 175105
